title: Migrating an old PackshotCreator studio to Orbitvu and its AI
h1: Migrating an old PackshotCreator studio to Orbitvu and its AI
metaTitle: Migrating an old PackshotCreator studio to Orbitvu and its AI
description: Is your old PackshotCreator studio still running? Latest-generation Orbitvu studios, built-in AI, support in France: migrate without stopping production.
author: Sébastien Jourdan
content:
“It works very well.” That is how a photo studio manager in textiles and childcare products described her old PackshotCreator studio this summer, nine years after it was installed. She is right. And since I took over PackshotCreator in December 2025, long-standing users of the brand have been calling us every week with the same question: should you replace a system that still runs?

Short answer: as long as it produces, there is no rush. But support for the old PackshotCreator software ended on 31 December 2024. More importantly, the current generation does what the old one could not: set the lighting, cut out the background and retouch product defects inside the capture software itself, thanks to built-in artificial intelligence. PackshotCreator, official distributor of Orbitvu studios in France and Switzerland, installs them, trains teams and provides support from its Lyon showroom.

Key points

  • PackshotCreator studios delivered up to 2020 run on Windows XP, 7 or 10. Their support ended on 31 December 2024.
  • Current Orbitvu studios load from the side, control up to 74 light sources and are designed and built in Europe.
  • The AI sits in the Orbitvu Station software: lighting setup, background removal during capture, defect retouching, reading product references.
  • On a 60-month lease, expect €270 to €490 excl. VAT per month depending on the studio.
  • The switchover happens without stopping production, with the old studio kept as a backup.

Your old PackshotCreator studio still works: should you replace it?

Let me start with something few sellers will tell you: the original PackshotCreator studios are solid. A jewellery workshop told us this summer that theirs had been running for six years “without a problem”. The mechanics hold up. So do the LEDs.

What ages is everything around them.

The software, first of all. The versions shipped with PackshotCreator studios between 2003 and 2020 run on Windows XP, 7 or 10, and usually not on Windows 11. Yet Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 on 14 October 2025. The day the PC that drives the studio has to be replaced, the software may not come along. A user in cosmetics put it better than we could: “with the old one, we have to change the PC, and then the software won't be compatible any more”. (Software lost, or rejected by Windows 11? Our dedicated guide covers the solutions.)

Then there is support. That software came from Ortery, a Taiwanese manufacturer that PackshotCreator no longer distributes. PackshotCreator support for these solutions officially ended on 31 December 2024. Ortery now looks after its European customers from its Rotterdam head office, with practically no local presence in France or Switzerland. As for spare parts, they get harder to find every year.

Our position fits in one sentence: keep your studio while it produces, and prepare what comes next while it is still producing.

What the Orbitvu generation changes in the shoot

The first change shows on day one: loading. Some of the older models opened through a front door. You placed the object at the back, closed the door, checked, opened it again. Orbitvu studios open from the sides. The Alphashot XL Pro v2 has sliding doors on both sides and a centring laser, the Alphashot 360 a double door. Over a day of 200 SKUs, every movement saved adds up.

Second change: lighting becomes a software setting. The Alphashot Pro G2 has 74 light sources, each controlled individually. On the Alphashot Micro Pro v2, designed for jewellery and watches, backlit LED doors draw soft highlights along the sides of a ring. Third change, less visible: product data. The Alphashot XL G2 photographs, laser-measures and weighs the object in a single cycle.

The AI in Orbitvu Station: what it already does in production

This is where the generational leap happens. On an old studio, every new product family meant trial and error: raise one zone, lower another, start again. On the Alphashot Pro G2, the AI lighting assistant suggests the light and camera settings suited to the object on its own, with nothing to type in. You fine-tune if needed, then save the template.

Version 26.2 of Orbitvu Station, released on 23 June 2026, added what was still missing:

  • AI background removal directly during capture, with the option to keep the product's natural shadow;
  • an AI retoucher, which removes stray reflections and imperfections, adjusts colours, and a good deal more;
  • OCR reading (text recognition), also in beta, which picks up the product's references, labels and handwritten notes from up to six images, so nobody has to type them again;
  • one-touch automatic exposure.

The retoucher deserves a closer look. Scratches, dust, a dented box, removing elements and so on: it fixes these defects directly in Orbitvu Station, and shows the product at its best the way a professional retoucher would, without changing the accuracy of its features. What used to go off to post-production is now handled at the capture station. And further, more advanced features are planned before the end of the year.

If you remember one thing, make it this: this AI works on a real photo of the real product. It sets, cuts out, corrects, reads. It invents nothing. That stopped being a detail on 2 August 2026, when Article 50 of the EU AI Act started to apply: an image that is generated, or altered to the point of showing something other than reality, must now carry a machine-readable label. Colour or exposure corrections and conventional studio retouching fall outside this obligation, as the analysis published by Orbitvu explains. It flags only one borderline case: adding shadows or reflections to a cut-out that were never photographed.

A European manufacturer, a team in France and Switzerland

Orbitvu designs and builds its studios in Poland, at its factory in Silesia. Mechanics, electronics and software are developed in-house, by a research and development team of more than 30 people. The studio and the software that drives it come from the same house. They evolve together.

In France and Switzerland, we are the local link. PackshotCreator installs and calibrates every studio, trains operators on site and provides technical support in French. Our training courses are Qualiopi-certified (the French quality certification for training providers): in France, the training part can be funded up to 100% by the OPCOs, the sector-based training funds. And the team that picks up the phone spends its days on questions of photography and AI applied to packshots. A reflection on a steel watch. A clear bottle that disappears into the white background. The kind of problem we have seen before, often more than once.

The difference from a manufacturer whose nearest office is in the Netherlands does not show on the day you buy. It shows on the Tuesday morning when a setting gets stuck and a collection has to go online before noon. Our Swiss customers benefit too: our Lyon showroom is less than two hours' drive from Geneva.

Profiles, files, camera: what gets rebuilt, what stays

Bad news first: your PackshotCreator shooting profiles cannot be imported into Orbitvu Station. They are rebuilt, in a few days, with guidance during training. Which, in practice, often turns out to be good news. How many inherited settings survive only because nobody dares touch them any more? Migration is the moment to start them afresh, and on the Pro G2 the lighting assistant can do the rough work.

On the file side, nothing breaks. Orbitvu Station exports to standard formats, RAW and layered PSD included, and its publishing profiles set the format, resolution and naming of every output. Your folders, your directory structure, your uploads to Shopify, PrestaShop or Magento: everything carries on as before.

The camera is not supplied as standard with the studio, because many customers already have their own equipment. Orbitvu Station drives Canon bodies, with a precise compatibility list: EOS R mirrorless cameras are recommended, while the EOS 5D Mark III and 6D DSLRs are excluded. If yours does not make the cut, we supply the body on request.

That leaves one special case, which we would rather tackle head-on. Our cosmetics user annotated her photos directly with shade references, and Orbitvu Station does not offer that tool out of the box. The need is hardly unusual: a very large high-end cosmetics brand raised it with us too. Our team developed a script for her that lets her mark the references directly on her images. It is one more string to PackshotCreator's bow: when the standard software does not cover a business use, we build the feature to order.

How much does an Orbitvu studio cost per month?

Trade-in and leasing come up in almost every conversation we have with long-standing users, so let's talk monthly payments. Indicative amounts, excluding VAT, over 60 months and subject to approval by the finance company:

Shorter terms, from 36 months, are possible. Before you decide, do two things. Ask for a trade-in estimate for your old equipment: it is done case by case, after a free assessment of your setup. Then run our return on investment calculator. In six steps, it works out your annual savings, the time freed up and the break-even point, compares buying with leasing, and produces a full PDF analysis. Use your real volumes: the figure it gives you is worth more than all our arguments.

Migrating without stopping production: the five-step path

  1. Audit of your setup: studio, PC, camera, profiles, volumes, and what happens to your files after the shoot.
  2. A trial at the Lyon showroom with your products, especially the most difficult ones. You leave with the files.
  3. Choice of studio and financing, trade-in included.
  4. On-site installation and training, from one to three days depending on the configuration.
  5. Gradual switchover: the old studio stays connected as a backup while the profiles are rebuilt on the new one.

Production never stops at any point. That is the only real condition for a successful migration, and the reason we talk about it while the old system is still running.

Nine years deserves respect

Our textile manager's studio has done nothing wrong. It is the world around it that has moved: Windows, support, and above all what capture software can do in 2026.

If this sounds like you, pick five products, the most awkward ones to photograph in your business, and book an appointment in Lyon. We will run them through an Orbitvu studio in front of you. You can judge for yourself.

Sébastien Jourdan runs PackshotCreator (Sysnext). A photographer specialising in packshots for more than 20 years, he took over PackshotCreator in December 2025.

faqs.question: Are old PackshotCreator studios still supported?
faqs.answer: No. PackshotCreator support for the Ortery software supplied with the old studios officially ended on 31 December 2024. The hardware can keep working, but PackshotCreator no longer provides updates or assistance for these solutions. Ortery now looks after its European customers from Rotterdam. PackshotCreator, official Orbitvu distributor in France and Switzerland, offers long-standing users a free assessment of their setup and a trade-in estimate with a view to migrating to an Orbitvu studio.

faqs.question: Does the PackshotCreator software run on Windows 11?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The versions supplied with PackshotCreator studios between 2003 and 2020 were designed for Windows XP, 7 or 10. Since Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 on 14 October 2025, replacing the PC that drives the studio is often when the incompatibility shows up. Orbitvu Station, the software for Orbitvu studios, runs on Windows 10 and 11 as well as on recent versions of macOS.

faqs.question: What does the AI built into Orbitvu Station do?
faqs.answer: It works during and just after the shoot, on the real photo of the product. On the Alphashot Pro G2, the AI lighting assistant automatically suggests the light and camera settings suited to the object. Since version 26.2 of June 2026, Orbitvu Station removes the background with AI during capture, keeping the natural shadow if needed, and reads the product's references and labels by OCR (in beta). Its AI retoucher corrects product defects (scratches, dust, dented packaging) and shows the product at its best like a professional retoucher, without altering its features. Further features are planned before the end of 2026. It does not generate fictitious products.

faqs.question: Can PackshotCreator shooting profiles be imported into Orbitvu Station?
faqs.answer: No, profiles cannot be imported: they are rebuilt in Orbitvu Station. Allow a few days, with guidance during the on-site training provided by PackshotCreator. It is a chance to review inherited settings and, on the Alphashot Pro G2, to rely on the AI lighting assistant. Standard output formats and file workflows (folders, naming, uploads to online shops) are kept thanks to publishing profiles.

faqs.question: Which camera should be used with an Orbitvu studio?
faqs.answer: The camera is not supplied as standard with the studio, since many customers already own their equipment. Orbitvu Station drives Canon bodies: Orbitvu's compatibility guide recommends EOS R mirrorless cameras (R5, R5 Mark II, R6, R6 Mark II and Mark III, R7, R8) and excludes the EOS 5D Mark III and 6D DSLRs. If the existing body is not compatible, PackshotCreator can supply a suitable camera on request.

faqs.question: Who distributes and supports Orbitvu studios in France and Switzerland?
faqs.answer: PackshotCreator (Sysnext) is the official Orbitvu distributor for France and Switzerland. Its team installs and calibrates the studios, trains operators on site (Qualiopi-certified training courses, which can be funded in France by the OPCO training funds), provides technical support in French and develops custom features when needed. Demonstrations take place at the Lyon showroom, less than two hours from Geneva, by appointment, or by video call for a first look. Orbitvu designs and builds its studios in Poland.

faqs.question: How much does an Orbitvu studio cost per month?
faqs.answer: On a 60-month lease, indicative amounts start at €270 excl. VAT per month for the Alphashot 360, €335 for the Alphashot Micro Pro v2, €445 for the Alphashot Pro G2 and €490 for the Alphashot XL Pro v2, subject to financing approval. faqs.question: Does production have to stop during the migration?
faqs.answer: No. The migration is prepared while the old studio is still working: audit, a trial at the showroom with your products, choice of studio and financing, then on-site installation and training, in one to three days. The old system stays connected as a backup during the switchover, while the profiles are rebuilt on the new studio. Production is never interrupted.
